It would be just as unfortunate if the statue of liberty was destroyed, or the Vatican was destroyed. I hate the Catholic Church and how they blatantly cover up priest misconduct but these buildings are amazing feats of art and engineering and we would have lost some of the greatest achievements of mankind if they were to go.

The Sistine hall of the Vatican library is absolutely stunning and La Pietá is a masterpiece of sculpture. I really enjoy Saint Peters’s Square and Michelangelo’s frescos. I think based on those examples alone, the destruction of the Vatican museum and the Sistine chapel would be a great loss.

No it doesn’t have the same meaning as the Statue of Liberty. Yes the church has hurt many people. I feel like that is irrelevant to the question of whether or not it would be a loss though.

The art of the Vatican has resonated, moved and inspired some many people. I think that is enough to feel upset or sad that it’s gone forever.

I’m curious though, I never understood the bitter hatred often found on this sub. Being a Christian seriously hurt me in the long run. My self esteem and feelings of self worth have been shot in the foot and are still just limping along years after my split from the church. I don’t hold a grudge though. Hanging on to that baggage has always been exhausting and stressful for me so I let it go.

I am not an activist but I will stand up for my rights to be free from oppression from any source and encourage others to do so, I just don’t see the point of being venomous though. Maybe you could help me understand your point of view?

Also when you think about it, most small arms are designed with the average Joe in mind. If a soldier can;t easily use and maintain his weapons with minimal training, something is wrong. 

I was never taught how to use my SKS, I figured out how to use it because it’s really straight forward. No training necessary for basic operation. Not I wasn’t taught firearm safety. I was taught by my dad and my cousin, though it should be common sense for most people... right?
